Stream: Go runs the operation in a goroutine started at the call and hands items over a channel, honouring callopts["signal"] (a chan struct{}) only between items; C runs everything synchronously before returning a List and has no signal at all.

answers.answer: direct returns a table and a second value that is always nil. (a) 2xx with JSON: {ok = true, status, headers, data = parsed body}, no err. A 204/304 or content-length 0 response gives data nil. (b) non-2xx with a readable JSON body: {ok = false, status, headers, data = parsed body}, no err key. (c) unreadable (non-JSON) body: {ok = false, status, headers, data = nil, err = cleaned error}. The error code is response_json_invalid or response_content_type, or request_status with details when the status is not 2xx, so a 2xx with an unreadable body is ok = false. (d) request cannot be made: {ok = false, err = cleaned transport error}, with no status, headers or data. A prepare failure gives {ok = false, err = err} without cleaning, and a denied allow.op gives {ok = false, err = string}. The second return value is never set. An error() raised inside a custom system.fetch is not caught by pcall and propagates as a Lua error. That last point is read and inferred.

differences: Accessor: lua caches the no-argument entity on the client (client:Planet() returns the same instance each time). elixir makes a new entity on every accessor call.
get_utility: lua returns a copy (Utility.copy: new table, shared functions, copied custom map). elixir returns the live utility node.

stream timing: lua runs the pipeline lazily, at the first iterator call inside a coroutine. elixir runs it eagerly inside stream/4 before returning, and the streaming feature's items are also built eagerly.
stream signal: lua accepts a function (truthy result fires) or a table with .aborted. elixir accepts only a 0-arity function that must return exactly true.

Failure channel: lua operations return (value, err) pairs and prepare returns (nil, err). elixir operations and prepare raise by default. direct never uses a failure channel in either: lua's second value is always nil, and elixir returns a single map read via Voxgig.Struct.getprop.
Call form: lua uses instance methods (client:direct, client:Planet():load). elixir uses module functions taking the client or entity (Demo.direct(sdk, ...), Demo.Entity.Planet.load(ent, ...)).
Deleted mark: lua ent:deleted() is a method on the entity. elixir has no per-entity deleted/1, only Demo.EntityBase.deleted(ent).

Standalone program: lua needs require("<name>_sdk") plus a package.path entry when run outside lua/. elixir needs no import but must run inside the mix project (mix run from elixir/) or via Mix.install from elsewhere.
surprises: elixir: Entity.fragment.ex does not delegate deleted/1 or mark_deleted/1, so Demo.Entity.<Name>.deleted(ent) does not exist. runtime-table.md lists `deleted (ent)` as an entity member, which is wrong for the per-entity module.
Both runtimes: a 2xx response whose body is not valid JSON gives direct ok=false with err set (unreadable_body), not ok=true.
Both runtimes: ctrl.explain = true is silently ignored (only a table/map is copied into the control), yet the old lua REFERENCE gives `{ explain = true }` as the example.
The old Elixir README contains TypeScript code blocks in two sections.

Both runtimes: direct's prepare-failure path puts the error in err without cleaning it, while the transport and unreadable paths clean theirs. Same in lua (Main.fragment.lua:300) and elixir (Main.fragment.ex:216).
The old root README's Lua quick start uses `sdk` without a require line.
